svg.text: transverters-store RF bridge: as shipped, and the two correct ways to wire the balun
Drawn in the listing's orientation: Input left, REF top, DUT bottom, OUT right. Your photos show the board turned 180°.

g.text: shielded pair through ferrite beads: two white wires inside one braid
0.3 Ω short: blob bridges the pad row
whites and braid blobbed together at both ends
shielded pair through ferrite beads: two white wires inside one braid
shielded pair through ferrite beads: two white wires inside one braid

svg.text: white inner wires (PTFE sheath), two of them
braid (outer shield), drawn orange
solder pad
factory solder blob
What is wrong now
Both white wires and the braid are blobbed together, and at the OUT end the blob
spills onto the pad row beside the 0 Ω link. OUT centre pin to OUT shell reads
0.3 Ω instead of about 100 Ω. The detector's two leads are shorted, so the bridge
cannot read the difference between the DUT and REF nodes. Everything measured today
was leakage: 35 dB down, and louder with the load removed.
Which of the two wirings to use
The pads decide. Unsolder both ends and clean the pads, then meter each bare pad:
near 0 Ω to the DUT centre pin = DUT node; near 0 Ω to the REF pin = REF node;
near 0 Ω to any SMA shell = ground. Two pads at the bridge end: use COAX-STYLE.
Three pads, one of them ground: use BALANCED-PAIR. Both give a working bridge;
the only wrong wiring is any two of the three leads touching each other.
Coax-style, step by step
Bridge end: twist both white wires together, solder to the DUT-node pad.
Braid pigtail to the REF-node pad. No solder between the two pads.
OUT end: both whites to the OUT-centre pad, braid to the OUT-shell pad.
Keep every joint clear of the four-pad row with the 0 Ω part.
Balanced-pair, step by step
Bridge end: white 1 to the REF-node pad, white 2 to the DUT-node pad,
braid to the ground pad. If there is no ground pad there, leave the braid
trimmed short and insulated at this end only.
OUT end: white 1 to the OUT-shell pad, white 2 to the OUT-centre pad, braid to ground.
Pass check after soldering (meter on 200 Ω, nothing connected)
OUT centre pin to OUT shell: about 100 Ω (was 0.3). Input centre to REF centre: about 50 Ω. Input centre to DUT centre: about 50 Ω.
REF centre to DUT centre: about 100 Ω. OUT centre to DUT centre: near 0 Ω. OUT shell to REF centre: near 0 Ω (coax-style) or open (balanced).
Then on the radio: open reference near -2 dB at 1.3 GHz, and the both-open run 25 dB or more below it. That drop is the bridge working.
